title: Carmine I NDE 5395
content: At the time of the story I was an agent of the State Police chosen to be in service to the Department of the Postal Police. On 19/06/1991 at 16:45, I was doing an escort service to a postal van. Coming out of an elevator, at the post office in Naples, I found myself in front of six robbers. One of them shot me in the chest. The bullet hit me at the base of my neck cutting the subclavian artery sharply, and hitting against the bone of the scapula it fell down cracking the first and second rib. The projectile was broken in two and came out from the shoulder blade. During the trip in a police car to the hospital, I was suffocating to death. I spoke with a colleague who tried to keep me awake, but, in my mind, the memories of my life disappeared with frightening frames in succession as the brain itself was emptying. When I arrived at the hospital, I went into a coma. They managed to stabilize my condition and, at about 12 pm, they took me into surgery. The next day, the second operation started at 19.00 and ended at 03.30. The previous day, I was more conscious, aware, and calm because of the need to redo the operation. When I was asleep, under general anesthesia, I saw a little light in total darkness and wandered towards that definite direction. I felt absolute peace and a feeling of well- being. Suddenly, an invisible force restrained me. I felt as if some people were judging me. The feelings were positive and negative, and I was in a state of anxiety. Then, as if by magic, that mysterious force that was holding me back was gone and I continued to travel. A very large light appeared and I felt a state of absolute well-being. The more I approached the light, the more I knew that my place was with her. When I reached behind me, it opened a beautiful vision. There were thousands of lights, the same as I was (I was a light) and all of them moving with harmony. I was happy because I knew that my place was with them. Then suddenly I returned all the way back at breakneck speed, and found myself lying on the operating table. My body was still asleep but I felt, that is I heard and felt everything from a state of anxiety. I witnessed the last hours of the operation until my body started waking up from the anesthesia. I was shocked by what I experienced. I felt the need to tell someone, so at about 10.00 a.m. when I decided to talk to the monk. He was often in the intensive care to bring comfort to people hospitalized. He very carefully listened to the whole story and then said something that upset me. 'Dear brother', he said, 'for 25 years I have been coming here and nobody has ever told such a story. If this is all true, it is great because, under anesthesia it's really impossible to dream.' Then he added, 'It is very likely that during the operation you had a crisis and they lost you.' At approximately 12.00 on the tour, I asked the medical supervisor of one of the doctors who was present at the operation, if there had been some difficulty during surgery. He was very hesitant but then told me that for a time they had lost me. So, I decided to keep that beautiful experience to myself. Now, after 21 years, I have told my experience to only a few people because there is a lot of skepticism. The only person who ever expressed belief was that monk.

person_demographics.occupation: State Police agent assigned to the Department of the Postal Police

stage_sequence.sequence_variation_description: Life memories appeared before anesthesia/transition; later movement through darkness toward light, restraint/judgment feelings, then larger light and 'thousands of lights,' followed by rapid return and observation from the operating table.

unique_elements.nonstandard_elements: He described a restraint by an 'invisible force' with a sense of being judged, which then 'as if by magic' released him; later he said he 'witnessed the last hours of the operation' while his body was still asleep.

I felt as if some people were judging me.”; “There were thousands of lights, the same as I was (I was a light) and all of them moving with harmony.”; “Then suddenly I returned all the way back at breakneck speed, and found myself lying on the operating table.”
